items.title: Knicks assistant won’t return to team after three seasons: ‘Best years of my life’
items.content:
Knicks assistantAt least one Knicks assistant won’t be back next year. 

Carson Shanks, who spent the last three years with the Knicks as an assistant, won’t be returning. His contract expired this offseason, according to a league source. 

He most recently served as the team’s assistant director of video/analytics and player development. A 7-footer who played college basketball at North Dakota and Loyola Chicago, he often worked with the team’s big men in warmups. 

View this post on Instagram“3 years of the Mecca, 3 years of the City, 3 years of being a New York Knick, and most importantly, 3 years of Memories and Relationships that’ll never go away,” Shanks posted on Instagram. “The Garden shaking and sharing it with family, the sounds of the city during the parade, the taste of that champagne, the feel of the Larry O’Brien trophy, things I’ll have forever.

“SO excited for what is next, but thank you New York for 3 of the best years of my life.” 

All of coach Mike Brown’s front-of-the-bench assistants are expected to be back next year, though there could be some other movement further down the pecking order.

But amidst the roster limbo the Bucks find themselves in, tidbits continue to emerge about one particular player of interest: Peyton Watson. Let’s catch up.

A delayed resolution?The news: Reports from Jake Fischer indicate that a resolution on the Watson front might not come until some time in September, with Watson and his Klutch Sports Group agent Rich Paul apparently “willing to remain patient.”

Why it matters: For the Bucks, this continues their roster holding pattern. With Watson the most talented player the Bucks have been linked to—they have also been connected with Jonathon Kuminga and Benedict Mathurin—they are unlikely to make any roster moves until this situation plays out. So, the roster remains at 17. 

Actively involvedThe news: According to Shams Charania, the Denver Nuggets are actively exploring sign-and-trade possibilities for Watson and the Bucks remain very much in play:

[The Nuggets] are in active trade talks with multiple teams on a Peyton Watson sign and trade. That includes Cleveland, Milwaukee, and the Clippers. There are combinations of player packages, pick packages as well. So either they’re gonna trade him, or you could potentially have him back on a 1-year, $6.5 million qualifying offer.

Why it matters: With the Nuggets seemingly unwilling to increase their offer to Watson and the Bucks one of three teams listed in talks, this is an encouraging sign. Of course, with the Nuggets becoming a second apron team after matching the Oklahoma City Thunder’s offer to forward Spencer Jones—and going deeper into it by signing Lonnie Walker IV—any trade will be complex (to say the least).

items.title: Takeaways from Jaylen Brown’s introductory press conference
items.content:
PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 6: Jaylen Brown #7 of the Philadelphia 76ers is greeted by fans for his media press conference at Francis J. Myers Recreation Center on August 6, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images	Five weeks and one LeBron James signing later, Jaylen Brown finally spoke to the media as a member of the Philadelphia 76ers. He answered questions for about 20 minutes about his relationship with the team and teammates, both new and old, and what he’s looking forward to bringing the city of Philadelphia.

The first takeaway of Brown’s press conference was the location. As opposed to holding it at the Sixers’ practice facility in Camden where the majority of these availabilities are, Brown requested that his introduction be held at the Francis J. Recreation Center in West Philadelphia with dozens of children in attendance.

The man of the hour has arrived pic.twitter.com/L3BvEV0rYQ

— Josh Grieb (@JGrieb10) August 6, 2026As someone who’s been active in the Boston community, Brown is hoping to have that same impact in his new city. 

“People who know my family and I, we are rooted in the community,” Brown said. “That’s what we hang our hats on.”

The Francis J. Myers Center doesn’t necessarily mean a ton to Brown personally just yet. He admittedly is still trying to learn the city with this as his first step.

“As I’m getting started on a journey, embarking on a journey here in Philadelphia, the introduction, the first impression is everything,” Brown said. “I just wanted to let people know in Philadelphia that this is something that’s important to me.”

Those kids got to look on with members of the media, family and Sixers organization as Brown described his reaction to the trade as well as his new team. Brown said he threw his phone across the room when he first heard the news, but has since been in steady communication with Tyrese Maxey, Joel Embiid, VJ Edgecombe and LeBron James. Maxey, Edgecombe and Embiid all reached out to him pretty soon after the news broke. James has been active in the team’s group chats since he signed later in the month.

A theme of Brown’s presser was his desire to win and belief in the Sixers’ ability to do so, but he also isn’t sure exactly how that will look. He wasn’t shy about the fact that this roster is going to take some figuring out with the amount of star-quality mouths to feed. When asked what he’ll be bringing to the team, Brown sounded as curious as the rest of us.

“I’m not sure completely yet,” he said. “I think we’ll figure out as time goes on, as we start to spend time with each other, get on the court, and have conversations, etc.”

items.title: Latest On Peyton Watson
items.content:
Appearing on NBA Today (video link), ESPN’s Shams Charania reiterated that multiple teams — including the Cavaliers, Bucks and Clippers — are pursuing sign-and-trades for Nuggets restricted free agent Peyton Watson.

Charania vaguely described the types of offers that rival teams have been willing to offer the Nuggets to this point and capped it off with an eyebrow-raising comment.

“There are combinations of player packages, pick packages as well,” Charania said. “So either (the Nuggets are) going to trade him, or you could potentially have him back on a one-year, $6.5MM qualifying offer.”

Reporting for The Athletic, Eric Nehm hears from sources that the Hawks are another team intrigued by Watson, as has been previously reported. Nehm also confirms Milwaukee’s interest in the 23-year-old.

As for what the Bucks might be offering in sign-and-trade talks, Nehm’s sources believe the team would be reluctant to part with a first-round pick in any package for the 6’8″ forward. If a first-rounder isn’t involved, Milwaukee would likely have to include a valuable player (or two) to pique Denver’s interest.

So what player(s) might the Bucks be willing to trade for Watson? Nehm wonders if Jaime Jaquez Jr., who was acquired from Miami in the Giannis Antetokounmpo blockbuster, could be included in those conversations.

However, there would be complications in that sort of deal, Nehm notes, since Jaquez is eligible for a rookie scale extension this offseason and the Bucks might not be sending out in enough money in that scenario to make lucrative offer to Watson due to their first-apron hard cap. The Nuggets also can’t take back any salary in a sign-and-trade unless the deal moves them below the second apron.

Either way, Denver still has several weeks to work through the situation, Nehm writes, and if a trade doesn’t come together, Watson could accept his qualifying offer, which would feature an implicit no-trade clause and enable him to his unrestricted free agency next year.

As Ryan Blackburn of Mile High Sports observes (Twitter links), the most recent Watson chatter seems to suggest his agents are focused on finding him a new team rather than working to keep him in Denver. That could be because he’s unhappy with his contract offers from the Nuggets or his projected role with the team, or a combination of both.
